summary: Lost Type's microsite for Riley Cran's 56-style didone, built in pastel colour blocks around the story of the mid-century lettering artist Mortimer Leach. A colourful circuit-diagram header leads into a comic-strip introduction of Mortimer and Riley. A flip card then switches between 'The Fonts' (feature rows with iOS-style OpenType switches, a cycling multilingual word, packages and an optical-size waterfall) and 'The Story' (a full biography of Leach). The page ends with every style name set in itself and credits on a scribbled yellow sheet.

instances.look: A white field covered by a 'circuit board' of pastel squares, circles and bars joined by thin black lines and arrows, with 'MORT' (black caps on yellow), 'MODERN' (thin italic caps on blue), a pink disc with an italic 'm', a green '2018' tag and a purple box 'A serif typeface in 56 styles designed by Riley Cran…'. A line leads on to 'This is the story of a typeface.' and angled cut-out panels: a caricature 'This is Mortimer Leach.', 'Mortimer was a lettering artist.', a photo 'This is Riley Cran.', 'Riley is a type designer.', then a yellow banner 'This is Mort Modern' and a pitch sentence that mixes widths, weights and italics
instances.ux: On load the header boxes appear empty and their lettering fades in; scrolling follows the connecting line through the comic panels to a blue 'Get Mort Modern' pill (links to Lost Type). No nav bar
instances.learn: Introduce the font as the meeting of two people (the inspiring lettering artist and the designer) in captioned comic panels: the first screens tell the origin before any specimen
